clue.text: Think hard on purpose

definitions.meaning: to ponder or weigh something up carefully, used as a verb
done intentionally rather than by accident, used as an adjective

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to concentrate and to act with intent.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to ponder at length; as an adjective it means intentional, so both senses share one spelling.

clue.text: Take no action to get right of the entrance

parts.note: a do is a happening or affair, so action can stand for it
O, looking like zero, stands for no or nothing

explanation.surface: Advice to sit tight and wait to be given the right of way at a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in answer order, not clue order: DO (action) first, then O (no), then R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: A door is the hinged barrier that closes off an entrance, so it can name the way in itself.

clue.text: A title I translated for a girl

indicators.note: translated means the letters are turned into another form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A noble title has been rendered into another language as a girl's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges the seven letters of A TITLE I.
explanation.definitionFit: Letitia is a female first name, so it names a girl.

clue.text: A rag-bag assortment of coins?

parts.note: old British coins were called bits (a threepenny bit) and pieces (a sixpenny piece), so a jumble of both reads as the phrase for odds and ends

explanation.surface: A purse holds a jumbled mix of loose change.
explanation.walkthrough: In pre-decimal Britain a threepenny bit and a sixpenny piece were everyday coins; the question mark flags the coin reading of a phrase meaning odds and ends.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a miscellaneous collection of small items, a medley of oddments.

clue.text: Appearing to be straightforward-but sly or devious

indicators.note: devious means taking a winding, indirect route, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone seems honest but is really sly or crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devious' rearranges the eight letters of BUT SLY OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in a sturdy, vigorous, no-nonsense manner, which looks direct and plain-dealing.

clue.text: Although it's quite rainy, carries a sun-hat

indicators.note: the phrase quite rainy carries the letters within it, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Odd advice: even when the weather is wet, someone takes along a hat for sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' signals letters held within quiTE RAIny; 'Although it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A terai is a wide-brimmed felt hat worn in hot countries for shade.

clue.text: Goodness! Father's swallowed by a fish!

indicators.note: the word for father is gulped down inside the exclamation, so it is placed within it

parts.note: oh is an exclamation of surprise, like goodness
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A startled cry as Dad is gulped down by a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowed by' puts PA inside OH.
explanation.definitionFit: The opah, or moonfish, is a large brightly coloured ocean fish.

clue.text: He's an expert on the pipes

definitions.text: He's an expert on the pipes

parts.words: He's an expert on the pipes
parts.note: suggests a skilled bagpipe player, but the pipes meant are water pipes and the expert is a tradesman who fixes them

explanation.surface: A tribute to a virtuoso bagpiper.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who fits and repairs water pipes and drains is an expert on household pipework.

clue.text: Nets cast beyond harbour in the end hold a gift from the above

indicators.note: beyond means the next piece comes after the first in the answer
the harbour word holds a letter inside it, so that letter is placed within

parts.note: a haven is a harbour or safe anchorage

indicators.note: the end of the word the gives only its last letter
cast means thrown about, so the letters of nets are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Fishing nets thrown out past a harbour eventually bring up a divine present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the end' gives E, the last letter of 'the', and 'hold' puts it inside HAVEN; 'cast' turns NETS into SENT, which goes 'beyond' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heaven-sent arrives as if dispatched by providence, a blessing from on high.

clue.text: Enough players to have a row?

definitions.text: Enough players to have a row?

parts.words: Enough players to have a row?
parts.note: a group of eight musicians is also enough to man a rowing eight, and a row can be read as a quarrel or a stint at the oars

explanation.surface: Asking how many people are needed for a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: A rowing crew of eight is called an eight, so a group of eight players could row a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of eight musicians performing together is a musical ensemble named for its size.

clue.text: A French nobleman returns to Scottish isle, to fish

indicators.note: to means the turned piece is joined on after the island

parts.note: Barra is an island in the Outer Hebrides of Scotland

indicators.note: returns means the words for a and the French nobleman are read backwards

parts.note: a duc is a French duke

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat travels back to a Hebridean island to go fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns A DUC into CUDA, which follows BARRA.
explanation.definitionFit: The barracuda is a predatory tropical sea fish with sharp teeth.

clue.text: Putting claw in socket, I twist this way?

definitions.text: Putting claw in socket, I twist this way?

indicators.note: twist means wrench into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes which direction to turn after fitting a claw into a socket.
explanation.walkthrough: The page shows '1' where the wordplay needs the letter I. 'twist' rearranges CLAW IN SOCKET I, thirteen letters; the definition points at the direction of turning.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning counter to the movement of a clock's hands is one direction of rotation.

clue.text: Post log? It's possible to do so!

parts.note: to post a message is to send it on, to transmit it
a log can be a table, as in a logarithm table

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a log can be mailed and is assured it can.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition looks back at 'Post': the answer means able to be sent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transmittable can be sent or passed on, so posting it is possible.

clue.text: Bluff northern MP creates problem

indicators.note: problem works as a signal that the letters are troubled into a new order

explanation.surface: A northern Member of Parliament causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' rearranges N, MP and CREATES. 'Bluff' looks like deceit but means a steep cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluff is a steep cliff or bank, and an escarpment is a long steep slope.

clue.text: Look at disgraceful lad's wicked actions!

parts.note: to scan something is to look at it closely

indicators.note: disgraceful suggests bad behaviour, here the letters behaving badly into a new order

parts.note: the word lad's supplies its four letters, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone is told to examine a boy's shameful misdeeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disgraceful' rearranges LADS into DALS, which follows SCAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandals are shameful acts or affairs that cause public outrage.

clue.text: Tinkering with automobile bearings causes shocks

indicators.note: tinkering with something means fiddling with it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a car is an automobile
compass bearings: S, E and S for south, east and south

explanation.surface: Messing about with a car's wheel bearings gives someone nasty jolts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearings' are compass points, here S, E, S; 'Tinkering with' rearranges CAR and SES.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone frights or alarms is to startle them, as a sudden shock does.

clue.text: The virtue of a card game

definitions.meaning: the quality of calm endurance without complaint
a solitaire game played by one person with a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone praises the good quality of a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm forbearance is a classic virtue, and in Britain the one-player card game called solitaire elsewhere goes by the same name.

clue.text: After car skid, turn it about to make a kind of circle.

indicators.note: a skid sends the car out of line, so its letters are rearranged
turn means the word it is read backwards

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: After a car skids, the driver spins it round and leaves a circle in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skid' rearranges CAR into ARC, 'turn' makes IT into TI, and 'about' is C (circa).
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic Circle is the line of latitude bounding the northern polar region.

clue.text: Being this shape I can twist then pass around

indicators.note: the pass word goes around the twisted letters, which sit inside it

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: twist means wrench into another order, so the letters of I can are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shaped like a cone describes twisting and passing round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twist' turns I CAN into NICA, and COL goes 'around' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Conical describes the shape of a cone, tapering to a point from a round base.

clue.text: Gem of an accountant given blessing in church

parts.note: CA stands for chartered accountant

indicators.note: in shows one piece placed inside another

parts.note: a boon is a blessing or favour

explanation.surface: An accountant receives a benediction in church, a real treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: The containment runs loosely: CH goes inside BOON (BO-CH-ON) rather than the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabochon is a precious stone polished smooth and rounded rather than cut with facets.

clue.text: Jute thrown over the sign

indicators.note: thrown over means tossed about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Coarse sacking fabric is tossed over a signboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jute' looks like the fibre but means a member of the Jutes, the Germanic people; 'thrown over' rearranges THE SIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: Hengist was a legendary Jutish leader who settled in Kent in the fifth century.

clue.text: Silly picnicker ants terrified

indicators.note: silly means foolish and disordered, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A daft person on a picnic is frightened by ants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' rearranges PICNICKER ANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic-stricken describes someone seized by sudden overwhelming fear.

clue.text: Play time.

parts.note: reads as a school break, but means the time or speed at which a musician plays a piece

explanation.surface: A call for a break in the school day.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the speed or rate at which a passage is performed is its pace.

clue.text: Flower fragrance, say.

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: an odour is a smell or fragrance

explanation.surface: A bloom's perfume, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword trick for a river, something that flows; the Oder runs between Germany and Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is something that flows, and the Oder is a central European river.

clue.text: Orders opening: of case and examines?

definitions.text: Orders opening: of case and examines?

indicators.note: orders means arranges, so these letters are put in a new order
the opening of the word case is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A customs officer opens a case and inspects its contents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' takes C from 'case' and 'Orders' rearranges C with EXAMINES; the whole clue also describes what the officer does.
explanation.definitionFit: An exciseman was a tax officer who inspected goods for duty, so he opens cases and examines them.

clue.text: Journalist 'goes to civic centre wearing creepers

indicators.note: goes to shows the journalist piece is joined on after the other
the centre of the word civic is its middle three letters

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter visits a town-hall centre covered in climbing plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes IVI from civic, and ED follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivied describes something overgrown with ivy, a climbing plant.

clue.text: When he leaves the old must be informed

indicators.note: leaves means the word he goes out of the phrase, so those letters are removed

explanation.surface: Once a man departs, the elderly must be kept in the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes HE out of THE OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: To be told something is to be given the news, to be made aware of it.

clue.text: Surgeon giving food to a dog.

indicators.note: to joins the dog piece after the food piece

parts.note: a bone is food for a dog
a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: Someone hands a bone to their dog.
explanation.walkthrough: A bonesetter is an old word for someone who sets broken bones.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonesetter mends fractures and dislocations, an orthopaedic healer.
